summary: Delegated access approval links expire immediately for some SSO sessions
description:
Issue summary:
Users attempting to use delegated access approval links (used by Support/SRE to grant temporary console access) see an immediate 'link expired' error even when they open the link within minutes of generation. This affects a subset of internal users and appears correlated with sessions created via our legacy SSO route (Okta session created by older IdP cookie path).

Impact:
- Prevents on-call engineers from granting temporary elevated access via the normal approval flow.
- Blocks urgent troubleshooting workflows for production dashboards and runbooks.
- Affects ~8-12% of approval links generated in the past 48 hours for prod-us-east.

Timeline and initial detection:
- 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC: First customer-facing report from Support noticing multiple failed approvals during an incident triage.
- 2026-03-10 08:05 UTC: Ticket opened by Maya after reproducing with a test account.
- 2026-03-11 02:30 UTC: SRE confirmed pattern spans multiple Okta issuers; not all sessions affected.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From console, request delegated access for user alice@example.com using the Support->Request A Grant flow.
2) Approval service generates a one-time approval link and emails Slack notification.
3) Click the approval link using a browser session that already has an Okta SSO session (created via legacy-idp redirect).
4) Observe page shows: 'Approval link expired' even though the link timestamp is within 2 minutes of generation.

Expected behavior:
Approval link validates the one-time token against the approval-service store and Okta session, then displays an approve/deny UI. Token TTL is 10 minutes.

Actual behavior:
Approval service returns 401/400 flow with message 'token validation failed: session mismatch' and UI surface shows 'Approval link expired'.

Relevant logs / errors (samples):
- approval-service (2026-03-10T08:06:12Z): WARN token_validation: tid=8f3b, user=alice, reason=okta_session_cookie_missing, issuer=okta-legacy-1
- identity-proxy (2026-03-10T08:06:12Z): DEBUG auth: inbound-cookie: OktaSession=; path=/; secure=true; samesite=None
- console-ui (2026-03-10T08:06:12Z): ERROR approval-ui: display_token_error: token=8f3b, user-facing='Approval link expired'

Additional context:
- A/B testing shows the same flow works when the approval link is opened in a fresh browser session (no existing Okta cookie).
- Suspected the identity-proxy is reading the Okta cookie but returning an empty value for legacy-session paths (cookie path mismatch + recent cookie path normalization rollout).
- This manifests as approval-service requiring an Okta session (for identity binding) but receiving none so it rejects token.

Notes on frequency and scope:
- Observed ~150 failures in last 24 hours (prod-us-east) out of ~1.5k generated links.
- Affected users primarily have desktop browsers with older cookie jars or have been SSO-redirected by legacy-idp shortcuts.

Next steps (investigative):
- Reproduce with impacted Okta tenant/issuer and capture full request/response using internal proxy logs.
- Confirm if recent cookie normalization change (rolled 2026-03-07) modified cookie Path or SameSite attributes for legacy route.
- Add detailed logging in approval-service to capture inbound cookie header and Okta session presence for failing tokens.

Proposed mitigation (temporary):
- Add fallback in approval-service: if token validation fails due to missing Okta session, permit a short-lived guest-approval UX that prompts user to reauthenticate with Okta (force fresh handshake), rather than immediate expiration.
- Revert cookie path normalization for legacy-idp route if safe and perform canary.

Proposed permanent fix:
- Update identity-proxy to canonicalize legacy and new cookie paths consistently and ensure SameSite/Domain attributes are preserved.
- Add a session-presence check earlier in approval flow that triggers a reauth redirect rather than token rejection.
steps_to_reproduce: Request delegated access from console for a user (Support -> Request a Grant).
Open generated approval link in a browser that already has an Okta SSO cookie from the legacy-idp flow.
Observe 'Approval link expired' message despite link created <2 minutes ago.
Check approval-service and identity-proxy logs for 'okta_session_cookie_missing' and empty inbound cookie values.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Maya Patel (Support): Reproduced with test user. Attaching proxy logs. Marking P1 due to blocked oncall workflows.

2026-03-10 | Liam O'Connor (SRE): Assigned. Initial hypothesis: cookie path normalization rolled 2026-03-07 may be truncating legacy Okta cookie on certain request paths. Will instrument identity-proxy to log incoming cookie headers for failing flows.

2026-03-11 | Priya Rao (Identity): Confirmed cookie path differs between legacy-idp and oauth-route. Related config change: env var OKTA_COOKIE_PATH normalization set in deploy 2026-03-07 (PR github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/412).

2026-03-11 | Liam O'Connor (SRE): Temporary mitigation implemented in approval-service to show 'reauth required' instead of immediate 'expired' for token failures tied to missing session. Canary enabled in prod-us-east (10% traffic). Monitoring errors dropped by ~70% in canary region.
2026-03-12 | Maya Patel (Support): Customers on Slack reported the reauth prompt allows completing approvals after reauth. Some older browser clients still fail due to blocked third-party cookies.
investigation_notes: Captured request/response trace: approval-service attempted to bind token->session, but identity-proxy sent 'OktaSession' cookie as empty string for requests with path starting '/support/approve'.
PR of interest: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/412 - cookie-path normalization change (deployed 2026-03-07).
Dashboard: grafana.redwood.internal/d/ApprovalFlow/approval-errors?orgId=1 shows spike starting 2026-03-09 21:00 UTC with error tag 'okta_session_cookie_missing'.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-11: Deployed approval-service fallback UX that prompts reauth for missing Okta session rather than marking token expired. Canary at 10% in prod-us-east reduced user-impact; monitor for 24h.
Planned: identity-proxy rollback of cookie-path normalization for legacy-idp route and a follow-up test across common browsers before full rollback.
